findings.issue_text: [High/bug] testsuite AssertEvents.java isAccessTokenId matcher return logic is inverted: returns false when the grant shortcut matches, so it only passes when grant does not equal expected value; should return true on match

[Medium/bug] testsuite AssertEvents.java isAccessTokenId off-by-one index: grant shortcut occupies characters 4-5, so must be substring(4, 6) not substring(3, 5); current code slices tail of tokenType plus first char of grantType, and the comment contradicts the code

[High/bug] AccessTokenContext.java constructor: rawTokenId is never null-checked due to copy-paste error calling Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"); null rawTokenId silently accepted, producing token id ending in ":null"

[High/api] Adding String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation is a compile-breaking change for third-party implementations; same for removing the Context(Context) copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context; needs defaults/deprecation path or major-version gate

[High/bug] TokenManager.java initToken: access-token jti no longer a UUID and now embeds context ("onrtac:<uuid>"), silently affecting code treating token IDs as opaque UUIDs (revocation-by-ID, Details.TOKEN_ID consumers, external clients parsing jti as UUID, admin events, storage keyed on token id); compatibility/impact assessment missing

[Medium/bug] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext: calling getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) dereferences session.getContext().getClient() and can throw NPE when client is not yet set (service-account/ROPC paths); also inconsistent since initToken has the client parameter available but provider relies on ambient session context

[Medium/data] OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java createTokenResponse persists the raw grant_type form parameter value into the potentially persisted client session via a very generic key, colliding with any existing note/attribute named grant_type
[Medium/bug] OAuth2GrantTypeBase.Context: grantType snapshot via formParams.getFirst(...) in constructor becomes stale when setFormParams(...) later replaces formParams without updating grantType

[Medium/test_gap] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java: no test covers getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext or an id containing extra colons; no integration test asserts actual issued jti format end-to-end, and event matchers themselves are broken so test suite passes regardless of real format

[Low/concurrency] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut: non-atomic read-check-put lazy refresh can cache inconsistent mappings across concurrent threads when duplicate shortcuts exist among hot-deployed providers; duplicate-shortcut detection only done once in postInit so later duplicates silently corrupt maps

[Low/doc_defect] OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java javadoc for getShortcut() does not document required format (2 chars, allowed characters, case) even though encoder hard-requires 2-char shortcut, causing custom implementers to produce tokens whose IDs fail decoding
[Low/bug] StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java: unused import TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory added while code actually uses OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE

[Low/bug] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java getTokenContextFromTokenId: a 6-char prefix without a colon is decoded with rawId == "" instead of rejected; and an old-style id containing a colon after 6 chars of non-shortcut content throws IllegalArgumentException instead of degrading to UNKNOWN, creating inconsistent handling of legacy/malformed IDs

goldens.comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] testsuite AssertEvents.java isAccessTokenId off-by-one index: grant shortcut occupies characters 4-5, so must be substring(4, 6) not substring(3, 5); current code slices tail of tokenType plus first char of grantType, and the comment contradicts the code

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), the token id prefix format in this diff is 6 chars: sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShortcut(2) (see DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()). Therefore the grant shortcut occupies indices [4,6) of the prefix. The matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which slices the last char of tokenType plus the first char of grantShortcut, so it cannot correctly validate the expected grant shortcut; the comment about “4th char and 2-chars long” also does not match the code. This is a verifiable correctness defect in the test code introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/api] Adding String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation is a compile-breaking change for third-party implementations; same for removing the Context(Context) copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context; needs defaults/deprecation path or major-version gate

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (no `default` implementation), which will force all implementers to update or they will fail to compile. The diff also removes the `OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context)` copy constructor entirely. Both changes are source/binary incompatible for third-party extensions using these SPIs, even though the Keycloak-in-tree implementations are updated in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] TokenManager.java initToken: access-token jti no longer a UUID and now embeds context ("onrtac:<uuid>"), silently affecting code treating token IDs as opaque UUIDs (revocation-by-ID, Details.TOKEN_ID consumers, external clients parsing jti as UUID, admin events, storage keyed on token id); compatibility/impact assessment missing

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes access token `jti` generation from a plain `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()` (UUID-like) to an encoded form via `TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)`, which in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` is `stShortcut + ttShortcut + grantShortcut + ':' + rawTokenId` (e.g., `onrtac:<uuid>`). Tests were adjusted to no longer expect `Details.TOKEN_ID` to be a UUID (`AssertEvents` switches from `isUUID()` to `isAccessTokenId(...)`), confirming a behavioral/format change visible to consumers. However, the claimed downstream breakages (revocation-by-ID, storage keyed by token id, external clients parsing UUID) are not shown in this diff, so it’s not verifiable as a concrete defect here; it is a significant compatibility/impact concern created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext: calling getShouldUseLightweightToken(session) dereferences session.getContext().getClient() and can throw NPE when client is not yet set (service-account/ROPC paths); also inconsistent since initToken has the client parameter available but provider relies on ambient session context

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, the new logic calls AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which dereferences session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...) without any null-check (see AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper change to public static). The diff, however, does not prove that this method is invoked when session.getContext().getClient() is unset; TokenManager.initToken is called with a non-null client parameter but the provider ignores it and relies on ambient session context instead, creating a concrete inconsistency/fragility introduced by this change, though the claimed NPE on specific paths is not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java createTokenResponse persists the raw grant_type form parameter value into the potentially persisted client session via a very generic key, colliding with any existing note/attribute named grant_type

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Constants.GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (i.e., the literal key `"grant_type"`) and then stores the raw form parameter value into `ClientSessionContext` via `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` (and similar spots). Using such a generic, standards-named key increases the risk of attribute/name collisions with any other code that might use `"grant_type"` as a session/context attribute key. However, the diff does not prove that `ClientSessionContext` attributes are persisted beyond the request, so the “persisted client session” part is not directly verifiable from the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] OAuth2GrantTypeBase.Context: grantType snapshot via formParams.getFirst(...) in constructor becomes stale when setFormParams(...) later replaces formParams without updating grantType

adjudication.rationale: In `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context`, a new field `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor via `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`. The class still exposes `setFormParams(MultivaluedHashMap<String, String> formParams)`, but the diff shows no corresponding update of `grantType` when `formParams` is replaced. This creates a real inconsistency risk (stale `grantType` vs current `formParams`), but the diff does not show any usage path where `setFormParams(...)` is actually called after construction, so a broken behavior cannot be conclusively verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java: no test covers getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext or an id containing extra colons; no integration test asserts actual issued jti format end-to-end, and event matchers themselves are broken so test suite passes regardless of real format

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a broken integration-test matcher: `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` returns `false` when the grant shortcut matches (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), and it extracts the shortcut from the wrong indices (`substring(3,5)` instead of the last 2 chars of the 6-char context, i.e., `substring(4,6)`). This makes the new end-to-end assertions on `Details.TOKEN_ID` incorrect. (Separately, it’s also true the new unit test file only covers `getTokenContextFromTokenId`/`encodeTokenId` and not `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` or token IDs with extra colons.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut: non-atomic read-check-put lazy refresh can cache inconsistent mappings across concurrent threads when duplicate shortcuts exist among hot-deployed providers; duplicate-shortcut detection only done once in postInit so later duplicates silently corrupt maps

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, the lazy “refresh” paths in getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() mutate two related maps (grantsByShortcuts, grantsToShortcuts) via separate put() calls with no atomicity across the pair. Additionally, duplicate-shortcut detection is only performed once in postInit() by comparing initial map sizes; later refreshes explicitly support “new grant type was deployed”, but do not re-validate uniqueness. If a hot-deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory introduces a duplicate shortcut, grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) will overwrite an existing mapping while grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut) adds a new entry, silently corrupting the bijection and potentially causing incorrect encoding/decoding of token IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java javadoc for getShortcut() does not document required format (2 chars, allowed characters, case) even though encoder hard-requires 2-char shortcut, causing custom implementers to produce tokens whose IDs fail decoding
matched_golden_ids: Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to a documentation mismatch around the grant type shortcut length/format: the golden notes Javadoc suggests ~3-letter shortcuts while actual implementations use 2-letter shortcuts; the candidate says the Javadoc fails to document the (hard-required) 2-character shortcut format, which would lead implementers astray. Same underlying issue: docs should reflect the real 2-char shortcut usage/requirement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java: unused import TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory added while code actually uses OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE

adjudication.rationale: In `StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java` the diff adds `import org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory;` but the shown code only sets `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE);` and does not reference `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory`, making the import unused in the diff context. This is a concrete, diff-grounded cleanup/lint issue, though the diff alone doesn’t prove it breaks compilation/build.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java getTokenContextFromTokenId: a 6-char prefix without a colon is decoded with rawId == "" instead of rejected; and an old-style id containing a colon after 6 chars of non-shortcut content throws IllegalArgumentException instead of degrading to UNKNOWN, creating inconsistent handling of legacy/malformed IDs

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, when there is no colon (indexOf == -1) it returns a new AccessTokenContext(..., encodedTokenId) so rawTokenId is the full input string, not "". Also, the method intentionally throws IllegalArgumentException when a colon exists but the 6-char prefix decodes to unknown shortcuts (st/tt/gt), as seen in the explicit null checks; the diff does not show any requirement that such inputs should “degrade to UNKNOWN”.
